parts.problem_md:
A music producer is working on a digital recording project. They need to understand the technical specifications of their audio files to ensure optimal quality for different distribution platforms.

The producer notices that their recording software allows them to adjust two key parameters when capturing audio: the **sample rate** and the **sample resolution**.

**State** what is meant by the **sample rate** and **sample resolution**.
parts.solution_md:
Sample rate and sample resolution are defined as:

- The **sample rate** is the number of samples taken in a second/per time unit **[1 mark]**
- The **sample resolution** is the number of bits per sample **[1 mark]**

parts.problem_md:
**Discuss **the trade-offs between **image quality** and** file size** when choosing a bitmap image's resolution and colour depth.

Provide **examples **to illustrate your answer.
parts.solution_md:
**Resolution**

Higher-resolution images have more pixels, which means they contain more detail and have higher quality. However, this also means they have larger file sizes, taking up more storage space and possibly causing slower loading times on websites. On the other hand, lower-resolution images have fewer pixels, which reduces the file size and makes them load faster, but this comes at the cost of image quality, potentially making them look blurry or pixelated when viewed up close or on larger screens.

**Colour depth**

Higher colour depth allows an image to display more colours, leading to better image quality. However, this increases the file size because more bits are needed for each pixel. Lower colour depth reduces the number of colours available, which can make images appear less vibrant but helps in reducing the file size. This is beneficial for faster loading times and less storage usage.

**Examples**

A professional photograph used for printing requires high resolution and high colour depth to ensure excellent quality, but it results in a large file size. In contrast, a thumbnail image on a website typically has low resolution and low colour depth to ensure faster loading times while sacrificing some quality.

> **[mark-scheme]**
> - Demonstrates thorough knowledge and understanding with accurate and detailed material **[1 mark]**
> - Applies knowledge directly and consistently with explicit evidence/examples **[1 mark]**
> - Weighs up both sides of the discussion with suitable examples **[1 mark]**
> 
> This is a "Discuss" question worth 8 marks. Marks are awarded using a levels-based approach across three assessment strands:
> 
> - Knowledge and understanding (up to 3 marks): accurate, detailed material covering both resolution and colour depth
> - Application (up to 3 marks): explicit use of examples to support points made
> - Analysis/evaluation (up to 2 marks): weighing up both sides (benefits and drawbacks) of higher/lower resolution and colour depth
> 
> To achieve full marks, candidates must address resolution, colour depth and provide relevant examples. Each property must be discussed in terms of both benefits and drawbacks relating to image quality and file size.
> 
> **[8 marks]**

> **[exam-tip]**
> Make sure you structure your answer clearly using paragraphs — ideally one for resolution, one for colour depth and one for examples. This helps the examiner see that you have addressed all three required areas.
> 
> For each property (resolution and colour depth), always consider both sides: what happens when it is high and what happens when it is low. A common mistake is to only discuss one direction (e.g. only talking about high resolution) without mentioning the trade-off.
> 
> Your examples should be specific and realistic. Rather than saying "a big image has a big file size", explain the context, e.g. "a professional photograph for printing" versus "a thumbnail on a website". This demonstrates application of knowledge and will help you access the higher mark bands.
> 
> Avoid vague statements such as "it makes it better" — always specify what improves (e.g. image quality, detail, colour accuracy) and what worsens (e.g. file size, loading time, storage requirements).

**[8 marks]**

parts.problem_md:
A student is creating a range of documents for a school project.

The student records a podcast about computer science.

**Describe **how an** analogue sound wave** is** converted into digital form**.
parts.solution_md:
An analogue sound wave is converted into digital form by:

Any **three **from the following:

- (analogue) sound wave is **sampled ****[1 mark]**
- …**amplitude**/**height **(of wave) is measured **[1 mark]**
- …at **set/regular time intervals** (e.g. a number of times per second) **[1 mark]**
- Each sample/measurement is stored as a binary number **[1 mark]**
- The binary number for each sample is stored sequentially **[1 mark]**

> **[exam-tip]**
> An example of a 3 mark response could be:
> 
> *Analogue sound waves are ****sampled ****by ****measuring the**** ****amplitude ****of the wave ****at regular time intervals****.*

parts.problem_md:
A logo is stored as a **bitmap image**.

Each square in the image represents **one pixel**, with three different colours being used in the image.

**State **what is meant by the term **image resolution**.
parts.solution_md:
The term image resolution means:

Any **one **of the following:

- Total number of pixels (in an image) **[1 mark]**
- Height and width (of an image) **[1 mark]**

parts.problem_md:
A student has a **sound file **that is too large to be stored on their external secondary storage device. The student **compresses **the sound file to make the file size smaller.

The compression method used **reduces **the sample rate and the sample resolution of the sound file.

**State **what is meant by the **sample rate** and **sample resolution**.
parts.solution_md:
Sample rate and sample resolution are defined as:

- The** sample rate** is the number of samples taken in a second/per time unit **[1 mark]**
- The** sample resolution** is the number of bits per sample **[1 mark]**

**Extract:**

- Accept an obvious typo for "more bits" that still conveys more bits per character (e.g. "for bits" for "more bits").

The **Unicode **character set is used to represent text that is typed into a computer.

One disadvantage of using the **Unicode **character set, instead of the **ASCII **character set, is that the text stored takes up more storage space.

**Give one** reason why it takes up more storage space.
parts.solution_md:
Unicode takes up more storage space as:

- Each character is encoded/stored using more bits **[1 mark]**

> **[exam-tip]**
> Saying Unicode has more characters available is not the reason for greater storage and will not gain the mark
> 
> Make it clear it is the number of bits per character that is greater, not just 'more bits'

parts.problem_md:
**Extract:**

- Award the first mark for "set/list of characters" together with any idea of being defined/used/represented by a computer system, hardware or software (e.g. "characters defined by computer hardware and software").
- Award the second mark for "unique binary set/code", "unique number" or "unique code" as equivalents of "unique value".

The Unicode **character set** is used to represent text that is typed into a computer.

**Describe** what is meant by a character set.
parts.solution_md:
A character set is described as:

- All the characters and symbols that can be represented by a computer system **[1 mark]** *accept: a set/list of characters (defined/used by) a computer system, hardware or software*
- Each character and symbol is assigned a unique value **[1 mark]** *accept: unique binary code/set, unique number, unique code*

> **[exam-tip]**
> A 2-mark describe needs two distinct points, so don't stop at listing the characters — say each is given a unique value
> 
> Make clear the set covers all characters and symbols, not just those for one language
